title: with open

fakeFiles.story.txt:
Once upon a time.
A robot found a map.
The end.

goal: In this lesson you will learn how with open opens a file and closes it safely when the block ends.
learn: Do your work inside the indented block
Skip manual close — with handles it
idea: The safe style is with open("story.txt") as f:. Inside the indented block, use f.read() or f.write(...). When the block ends, Python closes the file for you. Less chance of forgetting close()!

output: Message: Hi from a practice file!

changeOneLine: In the editor above, change the first open to note.txt. Press Run. The first print should show the snack reminder.

practice.text: Use with open to read hello.txt and print it.
practice.hint: Inside the with block, read into text with f.read(). The print goes outside the block — but still uses that variable.
practice.starterTip: Fill text = f.read() (indented), then print(text) on the last line.
practice.starter:
with open("hello.txt") as f:
    text = 
print()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if with open reads hello.txt and prints contents.

practice.text: Use with open in "w" mode to write bye.txt, then with open to read and print it.
practice.hint: In the first with block, f.write() needs a string with \n. The second with block already prints f.read() for you.
practice.starterTip: Try f.write("Goodbye!\n") inside the "w" block — then run and you should see Goodbye! printed from the read block.
practice.starter:
with open("bye.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write()

with open("bye.txt") as f:
    print(f.read())
practice.gradingNote: Pass if bye.txt is written and read back with with open.

quiz.question: Why use with open(...)

options.text: It opens and closes the file safely

quiz.correct: with closes the file automatically at the end of the block.
quiz.wrong: with open(...) is the safe pattern.

quiz.question: Where do you put f.read() when using with?
quiz.correct: The file variable f is ready inside the block.

quiz.question: Do you need f.close() with with open?

options.text: Usually no — with closes for you

quiz.wrong: That is a big reason to use with.

project.title: With Style Reader
project.desc: Using only with open, read story.txt and note.txt. Print both with short labels.
project.starter:
with open("story.txt") as f:
    story = f.read()
print("STORY:")
print(story)
